The Roman Empire, one of the most influential and powerful civilizations in human history, has a rich and complex past that spans over 12 centuries. The story of Rome begins in 753 BC, when the city was founded by Romulus and Remus, two legendary brothers who are said to have been raised by a she-wolf. According to myth, Romulus became the first king of Rome, marking the beginning of the Roman Kingdom.

During the Roman Kingdom (753 BC - 509 BC), Rome was ruled by a series of seven kings, each contributing to the growth and development of the city. The kingdom was characterized by a mix of monarchic and aristocratic elements, with the king holding significant power and the Senate, composed of patrician families, advising him on important matters. This period saw the construction of key infrastructure, such as the Roman Forum, and the establishment of important institutions, including the Roman Senate and the Roman Legions.

As the Roman Kingdom came to an end, the Roman Republic (509 BC - 27 BC) was born. The last king of Rome, Lucius Tarquinius Superbus, was overthrown, and a new system of government was established, with power held by the Senate and the Assemblies. The Roman Republic was marked by a series of conflicts, including the Punic Wars against Carthage, which lasted from 264 BC to 146 BC.
